rubrics.title: UC comprehensive review factors (first-year)

criteria.name: A-G GPA
criteria.description: Grade point average across all completed A-G courses, with extra points for UC-certified honors courses.

criteria.name: Courses beyond minimum
criteria.description: How many A-G courses you took beyond the minimum requirements, what they covered, and how you performed.

criteria.name: Honors and college-level work
criteria.description: Number of and results in UC-approved honors, AP, IB Higher Level and transferable college courses.

criteria.name: Eligibility in the Local Context
criteria.description: Being identified by UC as in the top 9 percent of your high school class at the end of junior year.

criteria.name: Senior-year program
criteria.description: Strength of the senior year, judged by the type and number of academic courses in progress or planned.

criteria.name: Performance relative to opportunity
criteria.description: Academic performance measured against the educational opportunities your high school offers.

criteria.name: Subject-area excellence
criteria.description: Outstanding performance in one or more specific subject areas.

criteria.name: Special academic projects
criteria.description: Outstanding work on one or more special projects in any academic field.

criteria.name: Recent improvement
criteria.description: Marked recent improvement shown in GPA and in the quality of coursework completed or under way.

criteria.name: Talents, achievements and leadership
criteria.description: Special talents, awards, skills such as other languages, deep interests, leadership or service, and other experiences showing promise to enrich campus intellectual life.

criteria.name: School-linked projects
criteria.description: Completing special projects tied to the high school curriculum or to school events, projects or programs.

criteria.name: Achievement in life context
criteria.description: Academic accomplishments read in light of life experiences and circumstances such as disability, low income, first-generation status, work, hardship, refugee or veteran status.

criteria.name: Location
criteria.description: Where your secondary school and your home are located.

rubrics.notes: Live current-cycle page; no cycle year printed on it. UC presents these 13 as factors it 'may consider'; campuses use the same factors but apply them differently. Descriptions are paraphrased.

principles.text: Write what you actually want to share about yourself, not what you guess colleges want to hear.
Give readers something new: check that the essay adds information not already found elsewhere in your application.
Choose a topic that reveals who you are and what matters to you.
Small, everyday experiences are valid material when they had a powerful effect on you.
Do not list accomplishments; develop one topic with specific, concrete examples that support your point.
Write in the first person, using 'I' and 'my', so readers get to know you.
There is no right answer; use your own voice to show your personality, background, interests and achievements.
Start early and leave time to prepare, compose carefully and revise.
Proofread for clarity; grammar is not graded, but errors distract readers from what you mean.
Seek feedback from people you trust, but the ideas and every word must be your own.
